reviewer.summary: The PR keeps Hindi and other Indic combining marks in `slugify_unicode` and adds docs and tests, but it introduces a regression. Emoji with a variation selector (U+FE0F, category `Mn`) now leave invisible characters in the id. The default `slugify` is unchanged, so default-config Hindi and Russian headings still produce `#_1`, `#_2`. The full suite passes (1185 tests, 52 skipped).
issue_asks: Hindi and Russian headings should get readable, meaningful ids instead of _1, _2, ...
Section links should be shareable and understandable
Improve the toc extension for non-English docs
Existing behaviour (default ASCII slugify, other unicode handling) should not regress
commands_run: python -c slugify_unicode probes on Hindi, Cyrillic, Arabic, Korean, ZWJ, accents
python -c slugify_unicode('❤️ Love') and markdown.markdown('# ❤️ Love', extensions=[TocExtension(slugify=slugify_unicode)])
python -c re-implementation of the old slugify_unicode regex on '❤️ Love' and '❤️'
python -c markdown.markdown('# Привет мир\n## नमस्ते', extensions=['toc'])

findings.problem: Keeping every Mn/Mc character is too broad and regresses emoji headings. Emoji variation selectors (U+FE0F, category Mn) are now kept while the emoji itself (So) is dropped. Ids start with an invisible character, and emoji-only headings get a non-empty invisible id instead of the empty-slug fallback (`_1`). Old logic gave 'love' and ''.
findings.evidence: `slugify_unicode('❤️ Love','-')` printed `'️-love'`, and `slugify_unicode('❤️','-')` printed `'️'`. `markdown.markdown('# ❤️ Love', extensions=[TocExtension(slugify=slugify_unicode)])` printed `<h1 id="️-love">`. The old regex `re.sub(r'[^\w\s-]','',v)` on the same inputs gave 'love' and ''. A combining mark should only be kept when it follows a kept base character, or variation selectors (U+FE00–FE0F) should be excluded.

findings.problem: The issue reporter's complaint is about the default configuration, which is unchanged. Hindi and Russian headings with default settings still produce `_1`, `_2`. Russian already worked with `slugify_unicode` before this PR, so the only code change addresses Hindi marks. The docs note that `slugify_unicode` keeps non-Latin scripts, but nothing says the default drops them or points users hitting `_1` to the option, for example in the `slugify` option description or a warning near the default. The scope may be acceptable for backward compatibility, but the discoverability gap remains.
findings.evidence:
`markdown.markdown('# Привет мир\n## नमस्ते', extensions=['toc'])` printed `

Привет мир

\n

नमस्ते

`.

findings.problem: This new test file duplicates most of the tests added to tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_toc.py: Hindi, Cyrillic, punctuation, and the default-unchanged case. Tests that read the docs file by string matching are brittle. No test covers combining marks on characters that are otherwise dropped, such as emoji variation selectors.
findings.evidence: Diff shows the same assertions in both files, for example `slugify_unicode('हिन्दी', '-')` and `'# Привет мир'`.

findings.problem: Zero-width joiner and non-joiner (U+200D, U+200C, category Cf) are still stripped, so conjuncts like 'क्‍ष' lose their joiner. The id is still readable, so this is cosmetic. The per-character `re.match` is also slower than a single compiled regex.
